Step 1: Give Appreciations

It’s simple: tell each other what you appreciate about the other person. By focusing on the positive aspects of your partner and of your relationship at the beginning of the discussion, you remind yourselves that you are fighting for each other, not against each other. A relationship check-in is about creating a habit of turning towards each other. Having regular check-ins signals to one another that your love matters because you’re making time to nurture it. What matters is making space to listen, appreciate, notice, express feelings and needs, and stay connected to each other over time.

“I appreciate [incident here] because [meaning here].”

“I appreciated when you took the kids out for breakfast on Saturday so I could sleep in because it shows me you are thoughtful and caring. Plus, it’s a special time for our kids.”

Step 3: Select An Issue to Discuss or Process

At this point, it’s time to take turns sharing any concerns you may have since your last check-in.

Key words: take turns.
